text:
alex: heads up — we've started seeing periodic 200–400ms latency spikes on large-context requests (>= 64k tokens) on ded1.

maria: seen it too. spikes correlate with sustained high concurrency and a lot of long prefixes. memory grows then drops suddenly.

ben: do we have a perf trace? iirc eviction churn used to show up in the timeline.

alex: attaching quick profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
KVCache: resident=38GB -> 68GB over 12m
Evict loop triggered: 2024-11-02T14:12:07Z
Evicted entries: 1243 (avg size 16KB)
Eviction policy: LRU
CPU stall (ms): 210
io_wait (ms): 45
```

june: @alex thanks. that looks like paging/compaction activity. do we evict entire KV slabs or individual entries?

alex: current implementation evicts per-entry (token-chunks) using LRU. allocator manages slab pages of 4MB. we suspect fragmentation + many small entries => reclaim doesn't free whole slabs, resulting in occasional big compaction with latency penalty.

maria: interesting — FIFO under similar load reproduced slightly different behavior: fewer compactions but occasional correctness blips (some cached KV for recent prefixes missing, causing regen and repetition).

ben: can you outline the correctness blip? logs?

alex: example sequence: model returns token A,B,C; on subsequent requests with same prefix, we saw token B missing from cache resulting in B' produced instead. logs show cache hit=false for KV key that should exist.

june: that implies eviction boundary crossing entries that are still in-use by running requests. do we pin entries while request is executing?

alex: we had refcounting but there are races when requests reuse the same KV pointer across threads; eviction can free underlying slab before refcount decrement completes. we tried a quick fix to bump refcount on read, but that increased memory pressure.

ben: so two problems: fragmentation -> compaction stalls, and race on free -> correctness. LRU vs FIFO tradeoffs: LRU better correctness in steady state, but churned LRU with tiny objects causes more evict ops. FIFO less churn but evicts potentially still-hot entries.

maria: hypothesis: eviction granularity mismatch. model caches per-layer per-token KV, but our allocator slab granularity doesn't align. if we evict at token granularity we fragment slabs. if we evict entire slab we may evict unrelated tokens for other prefixes.

alex: repro steps I've used: run 256-concurrency with 32k–96k sequence mix, batch_size=8, no prefix caching, let run for 15m. then run golden-checker compare on generated tokens. consistently see spikes at ~10–12m and occasional mismatch failures.

june: can we add metrics to debug: per-evict duration histogram, slab_freeable_bytes, slab_fragmentation_ratio, pinned_entries_count, refcount_drop_latency?

ben: also add eviction_batch_size and eviction_policy_name to traces. and mark requests with kv_epoch id so we can see which requests used which cache generation.

maria: quick mitigation options: 1) switch to segmented-LRU by slab to reduce per-entry churn, 2) increase slab size so entries are packed and fewer slabs get partially freed, 3) conservative pin-on-read until request complete (avoid races), 4) background async eviction off the hot path with backpressure when memory high.

alex: i prototyped (1) segmented-LRU keyed by slab_id -> evict least-recent slab instead of token. initial runs reduced compaction stalls by ~60% but increased steady-state memory by ~8%. correctness blips disappeared in small runs.

june: promising. but memory increase might hit Dedicated customers. maybe combine segmented-LRU + async compaction + pin-on-read.

ben: long-term: consider slab-aware allocator that can migrate live entries to reduce fragmentation (compaction thread) and make free safe w/o races (epoch-based reclamation).

maria: agree. also add unit tests that simulate concurrent readers + evictors with randomized timing. we missed that previously.

alex: i'm going to open an RFC summarizing: observed symptoms, repro, data from profiler, short-term mitigations (segmented-LRU + pin-on-read toggle), and long-term plan (epoch GC, slab compaction, improved metrics). will include perf numbers.

june: please tag eng-sre and product if this config needs rollout gating. also add a canary with higher observability (per-request kv_epoch tags).

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: kv-evict-experiment -> canary on ded1 at 2024-11-05T02:00:00Z. monitoring alert: kv_eviction_latency > 150ms for 3m.

alex: thanks. I'll post RFC link when ready and include the micro-bench reproducible script.

maria: thanks team. if anyone has other ideas for low-latency eviction (eg. probabilistic TTL per prefix) drop them here.

ben: small note — check network bandwidth too. eviction leading to compaction sometimes triggers IO with NFS-backed logs that amplifies stalls. prefer local SSD for KV slabs.

june: i'll coordinate canary and alerts. alex please include remediation runbook for immediate rollback.

alex: will do. ending thread for now, continuing in RFC. :memo:
